name: Compressed Bracket Sequence
description: William has a favorite bracket sequence. Since his favorite sequence is quite big he provided it to you as a sequence of positive integers $$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$$$ where $$$c_i$$$ is the number of consecutive brackets " ( " if $$$i$$$ is an odd number or the number of consecutive brackets " ) " if $$$i$$$ is an even number. For example for a bracket sequence " ((())())) " a corresponding sequence of numbers is $$$[3, 2, 1, 3]$$$. You need to find the total number of continuous subsequences (subsegments) $$$[l, r]$$$ ($$$l \le r$$$) of the original bracket sequence, which are regular bracket sequences. A bracket sequence is called regular if it is possible to obtain correct arithmetic expression by inserting characters " + " and " 1 " into this sequence. For example, sequences " (())() ", " () " and " (()(())) " are regular, while " )( ", " (() " and " (()))( " are not.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ $$$(1 \le n \le 1000)$$$, the size of the compressed sequence. The second line contains a sequence of integers $$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_n$$$ $$$(1 \le c_i \le 10^9)$$$, the compressed sequence.
output_specification: Output a single integer — the total number of subsegments of the original bracket sequence, which are regular bracket sequences. It can be proved that the answer fits in the signed 64-bit integer data type.
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
